correctness.rationale: Every length a+b pattern embeds one letter per full block; a constant pattern of length a+b+1 does not. Greedy matching across each permutation block gives a new block exactly at rank nonincreases; this yields necessary and sufficient two-sided pivot inequalities. Stars-and-bars counts pivot halves; strict rearrangement proves uniqueness of Q=P and reverse(P), and a strict balancing ratio proves the optimal split. The asymptotics follow from the unique highest-degree summand. The standalone verifier checks 768 parameter cases, 1,245,538 patterns, 56 independently constructed subsequence sets, 12 sharp-extremal cases and 441 balancing cases. Finite tests are separate from the proof.

originality.rationale: Relevant 2021 and 2024 primary proofs and 2025 SAS algorithms were inspected and six targeted semantic searches plus accessible own-claim comparison were performed. All closest mathematical statements concern general arch characterizations, global extremal bounds, or input-by-input algorithms, not the conditional all-alphabet P^aQ^b pivot characterization with unique permutation-order extrema and balanced split optimum. This is a best-knowledge originality judgment, not a proof of literature uniqueness; an unindexed equivalent specialization remains possible.
residual_risks: A published exact specialization to two phases may use another name or be unindexed.
General SAS characterization theorems might enable a simpler derivation than the one given; the claim is the explicit conditional theorem, not the classical ingredients.
The literature review is not an independent expert audit and does not establish global absence of equivalent work.

value.rationale: Permutation blocks are a canonical way to guarantee subsequence universality, and a single change of permutation order is the simplest nonperiodic perturbation of that benchmark. The result completely characterizes the missing language at the first unavailable length, counts it for arbitrary q,a,b and orderings, gives unique extremal orderings and an optimal phase split, and quantifies the unexpected order-driven doubling of polynomial degree. It supplies a reusable structural boundary between homogeneous and switched arch configurations rather than an arbitrary finite data point.
